notes: C runtime functions under the Windows x64 convention (args RCX, RDX, R8, R9; result RAX). Register offsets are Ghidra x86-64: RAX 0, RCX 8, RDX 16, RBX 24, RSP 32, RBP 40, RSI 48, RDI 56, R8 128, R9 136, R12-R15 160-184. Preserved: the non-volatile integer registers; XMM and flags are left unknown (sound, less precise). Every entry is a declared assumption.

entries.name: memcpy
entries.notes: dst[0, n) = src[0, n); returns dst. Exact only when n is proven constant at the call.

entries.name: strcpy
entries.notes: For a defined call (src NUL-terminated, dst writable and large enough, no overlap -- otherwise undefined behaviour): dst[0] = src[0] when it returns (strcpy copies at least the terminating NUL, src[0] first); the rest has an extent known only at run time: all other memory is unknown. Returns dst.

entries.name: strcat
entries.notes: Writes an extent known only at run time (strncpy with n == 0 writes nothing; strcat writes after dst's string): no memory is kept. Returns dst.

entries.name: abort
entries.notes: Never returns to its caller (C11 7.22.4.1): the paths through it end there. Uses no pointer it receives (observes nothing).

entries.name: longjmp
entries.notes: Never returns to its caller (C11 7.13.2.1, _Noreturn): only the paths after the call end; the setjmp side is not modeled here (an opaque call). Reads the jmp_buf rcx points to (observes rcx).

entries.name: strlen
entries.notes: Reads memory of unknown extent: the result is left unknown; memory unchanged.

entries.name: malloc
entries.notes: Returns a new block's address (no program data flows into it; fresh: never an address of memory existing before the call, the stack included). Heap bookkeeping is not program-visible memory (assumption).

entries.name: free
entries.notes: Assumes no use after free: the freed block's contents are not read again. Uses no pointer it receives on program-visible memory and keeps none (observes nothing).

entries.name: realloc
entries.notes: Returns a block holding the old contents: the same object as the old pointer, assuming the old pointer is not used afterwards (no-use-of-old-pointer-after-realloc); realloc(NULL, n) is a fresh block.
